properties.name: A swept file stops being reported as unobserved because a parent directory also claims it
properties.rationale: Reported by music_graph, verified by reproduction rather than taken as filed. The reporter graded it "harmless" for their own use, and the grading is what makes it worth fixing: the harm is not the wrong entry but the loss of trust in a field whose entire purpose is to be believed when it says something was missed.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
music_graph F10, reproduced and fixed.

THE DEFECT. `coverage.rs` matched each observed path with `claims_list.iter().find(...)` — the FIRST claim covering the path absorbed the observation, and every other claim covering the same path was left out of `matched_claims`. A design that legitimately registers `archive/` as a whole AND `archive/reco.py` inside it therefore got the individual files back in `unobserved_locations`, in the reporter's words "despite being right there in `observed`".

REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, on their exact shape: one directory artifact plus two file artifacts beneath it, both files swept. Both came back as unobserved. The test was written first and failed with precisely the reported symptom.

⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A WRONG NUMBER, and the reporter had the better framing so it is preserved in the code: `unobserved_locations` exists to answer "did you forget to sweep something". An entry meaning "a parent also claims this" is A FALSE ALARM ON CORRECT MODELLING, and one is enough for a reader to stop trusting the only thing the field was for. They said so themselves: "harmless here, but it makes the field untrustworthy as a 'you forgot to sweep this' signal, which is what it is for."

THE FIX: mark EVERY claim covering the path, not just the first. The COUNT deliberately stays one per observed path — two claims covering one file is still one file, and incrementing per claim would trade this bug for an inflated `claimed`.

⚠️ THE MUTATION THAT MATTERS MOST was the cheapest wrong fix: make the field silent. Emptying `unobserved_locations` also makes the false alarm disappear, and it is strictly worse than the bug, because silence reads as "nothing was missed". THREE cases catch it — a genuinely unswept claim is still named; a sibling that merely shares a path prefix (`src/foo` vs `src/foobar`) does not count as swept; and an EXCLUDED path does not mark its claim swept, since an exclusion rule must not be able to launder an unswept claim into a clean report.

VERIFIED: 6 cases, all passing. Three mutations, each killed by the right tests — reverting to `find()` fails both defect cases; counting per claim fails the count case; reporting nothing fails three, including both counterweights.

CONTEXT WORTH CARRYING: F10 is from §2 of the music_graph feedback file, which is FOUR sessions appended under one name. §1 (F1–F9, written against 0.20.0) was already triaged on 2026-08-01 — see `fact:the-music-graph-feedback-file-is-four-sessions-and-its-first-batch-was-fixed-long-ago`. F10 is the first genuinely open item in that file.
